title: Aurora oncall pocket notes — Evelyn
content:
Shift: Aurora (overnight) — 11:30pm–7:30am
Owner: Evelyn Cho (notes)

Quick summary:
- Two pages: 00:12 — serving-runtime high tail latency; 03:44 — tokenizer OOM on small dedicated pool. Both stabilized with fallback policies.
- Follow-up actions listed; several short-term runbook patches needed.
- Commands and notes that the next person may find useful are below.

Timeline & raw paging notes:
00:12 — Pager: serving-runtime latency spike (p50 ~ 120ms -> 350ms). Alerts from tracing: increased read latency to model artifacts in us-west-2-dcov.
  - Slack thread: #pager-aurora (pinned link in JIRA-5721).
  - Initial mitigation: moved traffic to warm pool (route fallback rule) at 00:22; spike dropped to normal within 4min.
  - Observed pattern: artifact fetches coincided with a burst of model-version rollouts from infra (see deploy audit).

01:05 — Noted increased error rate for a single customer route (cust-phi-23). Root cause likely prefix mismatch in routing config (temp override during canary). Hotfix rolled 01:20 to reapply stable route config. Impact: ~12 failed requests.

03:44 — Pager: tokenizer OOM in dedicated pool az-2 for model rwi-gpt-13b-8q8.
  - Symptom: process killed by OOM; autoscaler created a new instance but it returned crash loop then stabilized after OOM kill count reset.
  - Quick fix: set temporary memory-safety flag on pool to disable large-batch inference (command: /ops/pools set --id az-2 --safety-level low-suggest).
  - Note: customer-specific traffic was routed to fallback smaller-model variant; customer impacted but degraded gracefully.

Incident follow-ups (actions to close/incorporate):
- JIRA-5721 (serving-runtime latency): add audit step in rollout pipeline to throttle artifact prefetch concurrency. Estimated effort: 1.5d. Owner: Micah.
- JIRA-5789 (tokenizer OOM crashes): add preflight mem-check in pool startup that verifies kv-cache reservation. Also add clear guidance on safe-batch-size per model variant to the runbook. Estimated effort: 2d. Owner: Evelyn.
- Patch runbook section "pool-memory-signals": insert symptom list (OOM kill log patterns), emergency flags to flip, and exact commands to drain/route. Priority: high.
- Postmortem? incident impact <= customer SLA threshold; suggest write short incident note in JIRA then consolidate if recurrence. Draft by Evelyn by 2029-07-06.

Runbook TODOs (short actionable edits):
1) Add exact commands and examples: 
   - route fallback: ./infractl route swap --from pool-az-2 --to pool-warm-1 --duration 5m
   - set safety flag (temporary): ./infractl pools update --id az-2 --set memory_safety=on
2) Add a checklist for rollout prefetch concurrency: who to ping, expected telemetry spikes, automatic throttle thresholds.
3) Add page titled "tokenizer-oom: quick triage" with: how to gather core dumps, where to find model artifact size metadata, and how to reduce batch-size without dropping to smaller model.
4) Link to quota/capacity dashboard (we're missing a persistent link in current doc).

Commands executed (for future reference):
- look at recent OOM kills: sudo journalctl -u rwi-worker -S "2029-07-04 03:30" | grep -i oom
- migrate route: ./infractl route swap --from pool-az-2 --to pool-warm-1 --reason "oom-stabilize" --dry-run=false
- set pool safety flag: ./infractl pools update --id az-2 --set safety_profile=low-batch
- fetch artifact audit: ./artifactctl list --region us-west-2 --since 2029-07-04T00:00Z | grep rwi-gpt-13b-8q8

Observations / diagnostics to attach later:
- Heap profiles show a spike in resident set around 03:40 that correlates with a large 1.2M-token priming request — need to add telemetry to flag oversized priming.
- Trace shows model artifact prefetch concurrency peaked at 32 simultaneous fetches during the rollout window; cap should be 8.

Notes for next oncall / handoff:
- If you see the latency spike again, first action: route 20% of traffic off the impacted pool, not 100% — helps maintain performance for critical customers while we rollback.
- Keep an eye on the artifact-prefetch metric (prefetch.concurrent) — alarm threshold should be adjusted to 12.
- If tokenizers start OOMing, do NOT restart the pool repeatedly; instead flip safety flag and scale down concurrency on that pool. Re-provision only after mem checks pass.

Questions / open items:
- Who is owning the rollout auditing change? Micah picked it up but we need a PR to land the automation.
- Capacity planning: should we increase warm-pool counts in us-west-2 during rollout windows? (ops-sig discussion)

Backlog/ideas (low effort):
- Small agent that watches priming token length and rejects/rewrites > 500k char priming with a warning to client SDK.
- A dashboard card for "recent pool OOM kills" with one-click routing.

Personal reminders (Evelyn):
- Draft JIRA-5789 description tonight and add the kernel logs I captured.
- Pair with Anika next Tuesday to add the preflight mem-check to pool-bootstrap script.

End of shift handoff checklist:
- Updated JIRA tickets with raw logs: done for 5721, in progress for 5789.
- Slack summary posted to #pager-aurora: done (00:45).
- Left a note in Confluence runbook under "last-updated: 2029-07-05".

Quick rough sketch of runbook text to paste later:
"tokenizer-oom: quick triage"
- Symptom: worker process killed by OOM with kernel message 'oom-killer invoked' and rwi-worker exit code 137.
- Immediate steps: 1) Enable pool memory_safety profile, 2) Drain incoming new requests to fallback pool, 3) Collect core dump and heap profile, 4) Open JIRA and tag eng-sre/serving-runtime.

-- Evelyn
